t: Prince Pedro declared Brazil independent of Portugal in 1822 and ruled it as Emperor Pedro I.
Under Pedro II the monarchy held a vast country together, while coffee grown by enslaved people drove its wealth.
Abolition in 1888 cost it the planters' support, and an army coup ended the empire in 1889 almost unopposed.
dyk: Pedro II studied languages including Hebrew, Sanskrit and Tupi, and corresponded with Louis Pasteur and Henry Wadsworth Longfellow.
ev: Prince Pedro proclaims independence at the Ipiranga and is acclaimed Emperor Pedro I
Pedro I abdicates in favour of his five-year-old son
Pedro II is declared of age at fourteen, ending the Regency
The Eusébio de Queirós Law effectively ends the transatlantic slave trade
Paraguayan War begins; Brazil will bear most of six years of fighting
The Law of the Free Womb is passed
Princess Isabel signs the Lei Áurea, abolishing slavery
Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca's coup ends the monarchy

f.predecessor: United Kingdom of Portugal and Brazil
